request.skillIdea: Lightning Arrow ranger that chains lightning arrows through packs for mapping

introduction.text: . The plan was built and measured with Path of Building, so every number in this guide comes from the engine and names its profile. In the mapping profile the build reaches

total effective health. The goal is to clear packs quickly while the defensive layers keep the character alive between kills, and to keep the same skill from the first act to the endgame so that nothing has to be relearned.
The defence of the build rests on
evasion on the passive tree and on the gear, with resistances at their cap

. The passive tree is grown stage by stage, and each stage is written down with the order in which its nodes are taken. Resistances and attribute requirements are checked by the app for every gear tier, so a plan that cannot wear its own items is sent back before it reaches you.
The character starts the campaign with the skill alone and builds the setup stage by stage:
The item that matters most is the crafted weapon, a rare
. After the weapon, the upgrades with the best measured gain per cost are, in this order:

In the endgame stage the character takes the remaining passive nodes of the plan, so the strength of the endgame comes from those nodes, the gear tiers and the crafted weapon, and the way of playing stays the same.

scalingAxes.text: Lightning damage, attack speed and projectile count scale the skill.

playstyle.text: Shoot into packs from range and keep moving between them.

strengths.text: Strong pack clear: the mapping profile measures
The same skill is used in every act, so the character never has to be rebuilt.
The gear plans name concrete modifiers per slot, so the upgrades can be bought or crafted step by step.

weaknesses.text: Survivability depends on the defensive layers of the passive tree: total effective health is
Crafted items need currency, and some prices are not calibrated yet, so the crafting costs are only shown where the market data exists.

closing.text: In short, this is a straightforward build around
that is measured end to end: take the passives in the given order, add the supports when the stages say so, and craft the weapon first.

explanation.text: is the centre of the build. The app picked this setup by measuring the candidates in Path of Building: it compared the archetypes with the same budget, kept the one with the best damage and survivability, and then searched the passive tree for the nodes that raise the measured damage most. The explanation of every choice is in the sections below, and every number refers to a calculation instead of being typed by hand, so a patch can be re-checked automatically.

rotation.text: as your only attack against packs and bosses. The linked supports (
) change the skill itself, so there is no second skill to weave in: the rotation is to attack, move, and attack again, and the order of the steps below is the order in which you act in every pack.

detail.text: as soon as the first enemies are on screen, before they reach you, so that the supports have already worked on the pack when it arrives.
while the pack closes in; the mapping profile measures
damage per second for exactly this situation.
Move away from the pack before it reaches you and attack again from the new position; the defensive stats of the plan cover the hits you cannot avoid.
Finish the remaining enemies, pick up the drops, and check the equipment slots in the upgrade order (
) for anything that fits the modifier lists of the gear tier.

tips.text: Take the passive nodes in the order of the progression table; the stage tables name the nodes and what each one does, so the build keeps working while you level.
Add the supports at the stage that names them and not earlier: the measurement of every stage assumes exactly the setup of that stage.
Replace gear in the order of the upgrade list (
), because that order is ranked by measured gain per cost.

commonMistakes.text: Standing in the damage while attacking: the plan assumes that you move between strikes, and the defensive layers do not cover a character that stays in slow attacks.
Swapping the supports before the stage that adds them: the measured numbers of the earlier stages belong to the earlier setup.

mapping.text: Run through the map and attack every pack with

without stopping, so that each pack dies while you already move toward the next one. The mapping profile of this guide measures this fast clearing, and its damage number is the reference for what you should see in ordinary maps; if you are far below it, compare the supports and the passive nodes with the stage table first.

bossing.text: Against a boss keep your distance, attack with
and step away when the boss starts a slow attack. The pinnacle profile measures a strong single target and gives
total effective health there; if your boss fights feel much worse, check the resistances of the gear first.

positioning.text: Stay at the range your skill reaches, keep an escape path behind you, and move before the pack is on top of you; the order of attack and move is the one in the steps above.

strategy.text: Run the maps your build clears fastest and use the profile numbers of this guide as the reference for what is safe. The mapping profile describes ordinary maps and the pinnacle profile describes a strong boss: if a map modifier would push your damage or your total effective health clearly below the measured values, skip that map. Progress in this order: practise the rotation on easy maps, craft the weapon, then replace the slots in the upgrade order.

detail.text: Enter maps with the gear of the start tier and practise the order of attacking and moving with
; fix any missing resistance before you raise the difficulty.
As soon as you can pay for the base and the first step, craft the weapon with the crafting plan of the start tier and keep the checks of every step.

phases.title: Replace gear by gain per cost

detail.text: Upgrade the slots in the order of the upgrade list of the mid tier: Weapon, Helmet, Body Armour, Gloves. That order is ranked by measured gain per cost.
When the mid tier is complete, repeat the weapon crafting at the higher tier; take the nodes of the endgame stage in the order of the progression table.

waystoneTips.text: While the build is on the start tier gear, prefer maps with few modifiers; every modifier that cuts your resistances or your damage turns a safe map into a risky one.
After every item swap check the resistances in the plan: a missing resistance is shown as a stat of the tier, and it is the first thing to fix.

explanation.text: Buy the weapon instead of crafting it: choose this when the currency for the crafting steps is short. The slot guide of the weapon lists the modifiers to filter for, and the item then replaces the crafted weapon in the plan without changing any other slot.

Playing solo self-found changes little in this plan: it already names drops and one crafted weapon, so no trade is needed. Keep the drops you find that fit the modifier lists, and craft the weapon with the plan of the gear tier.

question.text: Why is my damage lower than the guide says?

answer.text: The guide numbers are measured for a fixed profile, so compare your setup with the stage you are in: the skill

must be linked with the supports of that stage, and every passive node of the stage must be taken. If the problem stays after these steps, compare your character with the guide stage by stage until you find the first difference, and fix that one before you change anything else.

checklist.text: Compare your supports with the stage table.
Check that every passive node of the stage is taken.
Compare the weapon with the modifier list of the weapon slot.

question.text: What do I do when a resistance is not at its cap?

answer.text: The gear plans keep the resistances at their cap, and the gates reject a plan that does not. Open the slot guides of the tier, find the slots whose modifier lists include a resistance, and replace the slot that lacks it first. If the problem stays after these steps, compare your character with the guide stage by stage until you find the first difference, and fix that one before you change anything else.

checklist.text: Open the slot guides of your tier.
Look for the resistance modifiers in each list.
Replace the slot with the weakest resistance first.

question.text: Which item do I craft first?

answer.text: Craft the weapon first: it is the core slot of the plan and the only slot with a crafting plan. Buy the base the plan names, run its steps in order and check the item after every step before you continue. If the problem stays after these steps, compare your character with the guide stage by stage until you find the first difference, and fix that one before you change anything else.

checklist.text: Buy the base of the plan.
Run the steps in order.
Check the modifiers after every step.

question.text: When do I take the endgame passive nodes?

answer.text: The endgame stage lists the nodes of the last level band: take the campaign stages first, then the nodes of the endgame stage in the order of the progression table, and compare your tree with the table when you are unsure what you are missing. If the problem stays after these steps, compare your character with the guide stage by stage until you find the first difference, and fix that one before you change anything else.

checklist.text: Open the progression table.
Finish the campaign stages first.
Take the endgame nodes in the listed order.
